# Optional decision rows: exact repair boundary

The repaired 367-case candidate exposed four failures among the 77 existing
ProcessPersistenceStoreTests. EF InMemory evaluates a non-nullable decision-head
join key after the optional head join and throws "Nullable object must have a value".
All seven independent mapper cases and all 23 PostgreSQL completion cases pass.
The current source and binaries stay frozen until execution, reconciliation and retention.

Correct the single result-query owner after retaining this candidate:

- Explicitly lift optional head keys to nullable Guid/int before joining generations.
- Explicitly handle an absent budget before joining its parent scope.
- Guard correlated allocation/child predicates against absent budget/head rows.
- Preserve the same indexed query and projection; add no early probe round-trip,
  provider-specific branch, InMemory bypass or swallowed exception.
- Add PostgreSQL legacy result regressions with neither budget nor decision head, both
  with and without an execution ID: the selected query returns null and the actual unit
  of work persists/replays its result.

Invalidated proof: all 77 ProcessPersistenceStoreTests, the 23 completion tests plus
the two legacy cases, and the nine registered result tests. Expected successor: 111 cases.
The unchanged 223 remaining pure/dispatcher/recovery/mapping cases do not use this EF
query; the 21 budget cases and 14 original-reader cases have no added strategy result.
Retain those 258 passing behaviors only if the complete source diff is exactly the
reviewed query and new integration-test delta, with documentation changes identified.
Repeat direct Persistence build, dependent standard outputs, full static enforcement,
architecture query review, exact discovery, source/runtime identity and resource checks.
No test-only workaround or broad-suite pass is claimed.
